why: how long a model read's asks before the last may go unanswered before each is taken for a stall and asked again, the last with the full limit (studio/read_limits.py, screen_grammar.codex_json): every stall on record hung to the 900 s limit while answered reads of the same kind took a minute at most

rule_why.since: the reader cap (two at a time, 8b4ddd4): before it five readers at once slowed answered reads to 579 s; a read that started earlier is not evidence of today's reads. A changed cap is a new regime only where it moves answered reads past the margin: 3 at a time (2026-10-28, 63 locate reads, slowest 27 s, median 16 s against 13 s at 2) stays inside it, so since holds; a cap that does not, moves since to it and is measured again
rule_why.margin: twice the slowest answered read of the kind: no answered read on record would have been cut, and one that is slower still loses only the short asks - the last ask has the full limit
rule_why.floor_s: a read never stops sooner than a minute: a fast kind's slowest answer (style 22 s) is too close to an ordinary slow one
rule_why.min_n: with fewer answered reads the slowest seen says little about the slowest to come: the kind keeps the full limit
rule_why.full_s: screen_grammar.READ_TIMEOUT_S, the limit of the last ask (screen_grammar.READ_ASKS) and of every ask of a kind without a row
